cards.text: The people left in Judah asked Jeremiah the prophet to find out what the LORD wanted them to do, and they promised to obey, pleasant or unpleasant. The LORD's answer: stay in the land, don't be afraid of the king of Babylon, and do NOT go to Egypt. Now Jeremiah has finished telling them every word the LORD sent him to say.

cards.question: Two of the leaders, Azariah son of Hoshaiah and the army commander Johanan son of Kareah, answer Jeremiah along with some other men. What do they tell him?

cards.text: Friend, they ASKED for the answer, PROMISED to obey it, and now they're saying it's made up. They claim the LORD never sent Jeremiah to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to reside there.'

cards.question: If the LORD didn't send that message, the men say somebody else is behind it. Who do they say is stirring Jeremiah up against them?

cards.text: Baruch son of Neriah, Jeremiah's own scribe. That's like the doctor telling you to cut back on cookies, and you decide the NURSE must have put him up to it.

cards.question: The men claim Baruch wants them handed over to Babylon's people so they'll be put to death or ___ to Babylon.
After all that, Johanan and all the army commanders obey the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.

cards.text: Johanan and the commanders gather up the whole remnant of Judah, even people who had come back from the nations where they'd been scattered. The group includes everyone Nebuzaradan, Babylon's captain of the guard, had let stay with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the man the king of Babylon had put over the towns of Judah.

cards.question: Along with the men, the women and the children, who else is in the group Johanan takes?
Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah get left behind in Judah.
The whole group heads into the land of Egypt. How far do they go?

cards.text: All the way to Tahpanhes, and the text says why: they did not obey the voice of the LORD. That's like typing the address into the GPS YOURSELF and then ignoring every single turn.
Here's the thing about the word of the LORD, friend: it doesn't need a passport. Right there in Tahpanhes, it comes to Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jeremiah something to do while the Jews in Tahpanhes watch. What is it?

answers.text: Bury large stones in the pavement
Break a clay jar by the gate
Wear a yoke through the streets

cards.question: Jeremiah buries the stones in the clay of the brick pavement at the entrance to ___ palace in Tahpanhes.
Then Jeremiah tells the people what those stones mean. The LORD of Hosts says He will send for someone. Who?

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The very king they were afraid of, and the LORD calls him 'My servant'.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will set over the stones Jeremiah buried at Pharaoh's palace?

cards.text: His THRONE, and he'll spread his royal pavilion over those same stones. That's like dodging your boss all week, finally finding a quiet spot, and your boss walks in and moves his desk right there.

cards.question: According to the LORD, Egypt will be a safe place from the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar will come and strike down the land of Egypt: death, captivity and the sword, each for those destined for it. That's like changing your number to dodge a bill collector, and the FIRST call on the new phone is the bill collector.

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will ___ the temples of the gods of Egypt and take their gods as captives.

cards.text: And who lights that fire? The LORD says He will. Then Nebuchadnezzar will wrap himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, so the place they ran to is just the king's JACKET now.

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will leave Egypt unscathed.

cards.text: He will demolish the sacred pillars of the temple of the sun and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt. That's where we'll pause with the remnant, friend, and their story keeps on rolling.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 4, 9 and 11 are discovery questions: the earlier cards provide no basis for reasoning out the leaders' reply, Baruch as the alleged instigator, the king's daughters, or Tahpanhes. That makes four of the stop's seven choice cards dependent on luck or prior knowledge, so most choice cards are not informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question depends on card 3, which is no longer visible. "That message," "the men" and "it" do not identify the warning about going to Egypt or the leaders making the accusation, so the question is not self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
